# Base Movement | Pilates Supply

Premium e-commerce marketing site for a Pilates equipment brand. Built as a
**dependency-free static site**: hand-authored HTML/CSS/JS generated by a
small Node script, no framework or npm install required to build, run, or
deploy.

## Why no Next.js / Tailwind / npm packages

This was built in a sandboxed environment whose network policy only allows
outbound access to GitHub — the npm registry, Google Fonts, and every image
CDN were unreachable. Rather than block on that, the site was built with
zero runtime dependencies: plain HTML/CSS/JS, generated by a build script
that uses only Node's standard library. On a normal machine (with npm
access) you're free to introduce a real framework later — nothing here
requires the static-site approach going forward, it was a constraint of the
build environment, not a design goal in itself.

## Getting started

```bash
npm run build   # generates the static site into /public from /src
npm run serve   # serves /public at http://localhost:8080 (uses the global `http-server`)
```

There's nothing to `npm install` — both scripts run on Node's built-ins plus
the globally available `http-server`.

## Project structure

```
src/
  data/
    i18n/pt.json       PT-PT copy (default locale)
    i18n/en.json       EN copy
    products.json      Product + accessory data (specs, pricing, finishes)
    categories.json    Category metadata (names, slugs, routing)
  templates/
    layout.mjs         <head>/<body> shell, meta tags, JSON-LD, hreflang
    header.mjs / footer.mjs
    routes.mjs          Canonical PT/EN path builder — the language switcher
                         depends on this staying in sync with pageId/param
    icons.mjs           Hand-authored line icons (no icon package available)
    glyphs.mjs / art.mjs  Placeholder "photography" (see below)
    pages/*.mjs         One template per page type
  assets/
    css/*.css           Source partials, concatenated by the build into
                         public/assets/css/main.css (see scripts/build.mjs
                         for the concat order — edit the partials, not the
                         compiled file)
    js/main.js           All interactivity: header scroll state, mobile
                         menu, language dropdown, FAQ accordion, scroll
                         reveal, parallax, product gallery, lightbox, forms
scripts/build.mjs        The static site generator
public/                  Generated output — this is what you deploy
```

## Placeholder content — replace before launch

- **Logo**: no logo file was supplied, so the header/footer use a
  typographic wordmark (`.brand-logo` in `src/assets/css/logo.css`). Swap
  in the real mark by replacing that markup (in `header.mjs`/`footer.mjs`)
  and/or `public/favicon.svg`.
- **Photography**: product/category/accessory imagery is real supplier
  catalog photography (processed into `src/assets/img/products/`, served
  via the `photo()` helper in `src/templates/media.mjs` with a build-time
  dimensions manifest in `src/data/images.json`). The homepage hero and
  final-CTA backdrop still use the abstract line-art treatment
  (`src/templates/art.mjs`) — swap those for real studio lifestyle
  photography when a shoot happens; catalog product-on-white shots would
  cheapen the hero.
- **Contact form**: client-side validation and a success state are wired
  up, but submission doesn't hit a real backend yet — see the `TODO` in
  `src/assets/js/main.js` (`initForms`). Wire it to Formspree, a
  serverless function, or the studio's CRM.
- **SITE_URL**: `src/templates/config.mjs` has a placeholder production
  domain (`https://www.basemovement.pt`) used for canonical URLs, hreflang,
  sitemap.xml and JSON-LD — update it once the real domain is set.
- **Pricing/specs**: dimensions and materials in `src/data/products.json`
  come from the supplier catalog; prices, lead times and warranty terms
  are illustrative — confirm before launch.
- Each category currently ships one flagship model (matching how the brand
  is positioned — a curated line, not a large SKU catalogue). Add more
  products by extending `src/data/products.json`; the build script and
  templates already handle an arbitrary number of products per category.

## i18n

Portuguese (pt-PT, **not** Brazilian) is the default/unprefixed locale;
English lives under `/en/`. Both trees are generated from the same
templates/data, so adding a new page automatically gets both locales as
long as `routes.mjs` has an entry for it. `src/data/i18n/{pt,en}.json` hold
all UI copy — keep their key structure in sync when editing one.

## Notes on the build

- CSS is hand-written (no Tailwind) using CSS custom properties as design
  tokens (`src/assets/css/tokens.css`) — brand palette, type scale, spacing
  scale, easing curves.
- Animations are vanilla `IntersectionObserver` (scroll reveal) +
  CSS transitions. Reveal styles only apply once a `.js` class (set by an
  inline head script) confirms JS is active, so content stays fully
  visible for no-JS users/crawlers instead of being hidden-by-default.
- `prefers-reduced-motion` is respected globally.
